subject: Numeracy
title: Full, half and empty
objectives: Children will say full, half full and empty.
Children will fill and pour with cups and jugs.
content: Full and empty, half full, and pouring and filling.
teachingActivities: Use water, sand and rice outdoors or over a tray; mark half with a line or a sticker; compare tall and wide containers; let children pour, fill and empty at will; say "full", "half full" and "empty"; talk about which holds more.
learnerActivities: Say full, half full and empty and fill and pour with cups and jugs.
resources: Stickers or tape to mark half
assessment: Observe whether each child says full or empty and finds a half-full container.
expectedOutcomes: Says full or empty for a container.

lessons.title: Full and empty
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say full and empty for containers.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weights and use a balance.
lessons.starter: Show a full cup and an empty cup and say "This cup is full. This cup is empty."
teacherActivities: Pour water into a cup until it is full.
Pour the water out and say empty.
Let each child fill and empty a cup.
learnerActivities: Child fills and empties a cup.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour water into a cup until it is full. Children: Children watch and say full.
Step 2. Teacher: Pour the water out and say empty. Children: Children say empty.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child fill and empty a cup. Children: Child fills and empties a cup.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Is it full or empty?" Children: Child says full or empty.

practical.title: Fill and empty
practical.safety: Use shallow water in a tray and wipe spills at once. Supervise closely and use a towel on the floor to prevent slipping.

differentiation.support: Fill the cup together and say full.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to fill three cups to full.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Dry the tray and say full and empty.
lessons.homeConnection: Fill and empty cups in the bath or sink.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say full and empty for containers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Half full
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find containers that are half full.
successCriteria: Fills a cup to a line
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weights and use a balance.
resources: Cups marked with a line at half
lessons.starter: Show a cup filled to the line and say "This cup is half full. It is not full and not empty."
teacherActivities: Pour water to the line and say half full.
Compare full, half full and empty cups.
Let each child fill a cup to the line.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour water to the line and say half full. Children: Children say half full.
Step 2. Teacher: Compare full, half full and empty cups. Children: Children point to each.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child fill a cup to the line. Children: Child fills to the line.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Is it half full?" Children: Child says yes or no.

practical.title: Fill to the line
practical.safety: Use shallow water in a tray and wipe spills at once. Supervise closely.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find half full without a line.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the cup full or half full?

expectedOutcomes: Fills a cup to a line
lessons.conclusion: Dry the tray and say half full.
lessons.homeConnection: Fill a cup half full at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find containers that are half full" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Pouring and filling
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will pour from one container to another and say which holds more.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weights and use a balance.
resources: A tray of rice or water
lessons.starter: Show two containers and say "Which holds more? Let us pour and find out."
teacherActivities: Pour from a small cup into a big jug and count the cups.
Compare how many cups fill each container.
Let children pour rice or water between containers.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour from a small cup into a big jug and count the cups. Children: Children count the cups.
Step 2. Teacher: Compare how many cups fill each container. Children: Child says which holds more.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children pour rice or water between containers. Children: Child pours carefully.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which holds more?" Children: Child points to the container.

practical.title: Pour and compare
steps: Pour from a cup into a jug.
practical.safety: Use a tray for spills and wipe up at once. Keep rice away from mouths and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Pour with a funnel and count together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to predict before pouring.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups fill the jug?

lessons.conclusion: Dry the tray and say holds more.
lessons.homeConnection: Pour water between containers at bath time.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "pour from one container to another and say which holds more" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Water play measuring
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use cups to fill a bucket and count how many cups it takes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weights and use a balance.
lessons.starter: Say "How many cups of water will fill the bucket? Let us count as we pour."
teacherActivities: Pour one cup at a time into the bucket and count.
Stop when the bucket is full.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour one cup at a time into the bucket and count. Children: Children count the cups.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop when the bucket is full. Children: Children say full.
Step 3. Teacher: Compare with a smaller bucket. Children: Child says which needs more.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "It took ten cups." Children: Children repeat the number.

practical.title: Fill the bucket
steps: Pour into the bucket and count.
practical.safety: Use a shallow bucket outdoors or on a tray and wipe spills. Supervise closely near water.

differentiation.support: Pour with the child and count together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find which bucket needs fewer cups.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups did it take?

expectedOutcomes: Counts cups to fill a bucket
lessons.conclusion: Empty the bucket outside and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Count cups of water to fill a bowl.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use cups to fill a bucket and count how many cups it takes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 capacity check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child talks about full, half and empty.
successCriteria: Says full, half full and empty
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can compare weights and use a balance.
lessons.starter: Sing the full and empty song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: full and empty, half full and pouring.
At each station ask "Is it full?" and watch.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: full and empty, half full and pouring. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Is it full?" and watch. Children: Child answers and pours.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Capacity stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and wipe spills at once. Use shallow water and towels on the floor.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two cups.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to order three containers by capacity.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says full and empty; finds half full; pours carefully; says which holds more.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing with water and containers at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child talks about full, half and empty" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
